question: Steroids are indicated in all of the following forms of tuberculosis except:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Tuberculous meningitis" -> "inflammation of meninges" -> "steroids reduce inflammation" -> "steroids indicated" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Tuberculous pericarditis" -> "inflammation of pericardium" -> "steroids reduce inflammation" -> "steroids indicated" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Ileo-caecal tuberculosis" -> "localized intestinal infection" -> "steroids not typically used" -> "steroids not indicated" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Adrenal tuberculosis" -> "adrenal gland involvement" -> "steroids mimic adrenal hormones" -> "steroids not primarily for inflammation" -> "steroids not indicated" -> 80%
analysis: In the management of tuberculosis, steroids are used as adjunctive therapy in certain forms where inflammation plays a significant role in the disease's morbidity. Tuberculous meningitis and pericarditis are conditions where inflammation can lead to severe complications, and steroids are used to reduce this inflammation. In ileo-caecal tuberculosis, the primary treatment is anti-tubercular drugs, and steroids are not typically indicated as the condition is a localized intestinal infection without the same inflammatory complications. In adrenal tuberculosis, while steroids may be used to replace adrenal hormones if the gland is destroyed, they are not used to treat inflammation. Therefore, the most likely correct answer, based on standard medical knowledge, is that steroids are not indicated in ileo-caecal tuberculosis.
